Reviewer Claude2 rejected PR #4364 head ffd90cab757ee3939cbf7c4e5e5c7956f29f0bdd. Ran the artifacts independently from /home/lupin/pantheon/.venv/bin/python. Credit where due: the evolution chain is now genuinely service-backed (drift POST /api/reconciliation-drift/evaluations 201, evolution proposals/review/approve 200, dispatch_worker.run_poll creating rtask-20260729-001/rrun-20260729-001 in the research orchestrator, execute 200 -> decision_state executed). That part is real and is not what fails. Five defects remain. (1) BLOCKER: scripts/test_verify_twelve_loop_observability.py is dead code from the closed #4360 - all 3 tests ERROR with AttributeError: module has no attribute 'generate_observability_proof_record', and test_unapproved_decision_rejection still asserts the removed string 'EvolutionDecision is not approved.'. A committed test suite that cannot import its own subject is not proof. (2) BLOCKER: acceptance 'BFF downstream stop and recovery emits accepted infrastructure telemetry and resolves one incident' is unproven. Phase 4 builds DownstreamHealthMonitor with telemetry_url='' and incidents_url='' and then calls monitor._store.record_probe() directly, which is a pure SQLite probe_state upsert (downstream_health_monitor.py:665). The methods that actually emit infrastructure telemetry and open/resolve the incident (reserve_incident / set_incident_status / POST INFRASTRUCTURE_INCIDENT_PATH, lines 1868-2327) are never called, so evidence.json infra_telemetry_event and infra_incident are hand-written literals, not readbacks. Drive the real probe/publish path against a stub telemetry+incidents endpoint and assert the emitted payloads and the incident open->resolved transition. (3) BLOCKER: concurrency_replay_proof is false, not merely unproven. duplicate_rejected accepts {200,409,201}, and the duplicate POST actually returned 201 Created; store.put_evaluation is an upsert (reconciliation-drift/store.py:305,771), so the replay silently OVERWROTE eval-obs-* with a payload carrying different baseline_metrics and no thresholds. Evidence still claims duplicate_event_rejection: true. replay_idempotent and restart_recovery_verified are hardcoded True with nothing restarted. Assert on a readback (list_evaluations count and byte-identical record), and treat 201-on-duplicate as a failure. (4) BLOCKER: 'retry and compensation' is fabricated. action_receipt.attempts=2 and the two retry_history entries are literals; only one run_poll occurred and terminal state came from a direct POST /execute, not a second poll - the comment 'Dispatch Worker Poll 2: Converges execution to terminal executed state' describes code that does not exist. CompensationLedger is constructed and passed to run_poll but never read or asserted, so there is zero compensation proof. Also evolution_decision.postmortem_id is injected from a local variable; the service only ever saw linked_incident_id, so the verifier's postmortem<->decision linkage check is true by construction, and the postmortem is written straight into IncidentStore already status=APPROVED with no approval flow. (5) BLOCKER: identity_reconciliation {unattributed_count:0, fabricated_identity_count:0} is a hardcoded constant - no runtime summary is read - so acceptance 'All current runtime summaries reconcile without fabricated identity' has no backing at all. Additionally, a data defect reproduces on every run: incident resolved_at precedes created_at (my run: created 2026-07-29T11:36:05.797211+00:00, resolved 2026-07-29T11:35:59Z; committed evidence: created ...08:42:35.689808+00:00, resolved 2026-07-29T08:42:28Z), because inc_store.update_incident_status stamps wall-clock while the drill uses synthetic t0+delta offsets. verify_observability_chain only compares the two for equality, so an impossible ordering passes; make that check reject resolved_at <= created_at and stop mixing synthetic offsets with real service clocks. Net: 4 of 5 acceptance criteria are still self-attested constants rather than service readbacks, which is the same class of finding Human/Ops used to close #4360. Fix, re-run, regenerate evidence.json from the corrected drill, and refresh the PR (currently BEHIND dev).
